item.title: Letter: Thank you, Albert Lea!
item.description: Our hearts are full from the MLK Jr. Day Celebration at Riverland Community College. A huge thank you to everyone who joined us to honor Dr. King’s legacy.

item.title: Letter: Can we all meet in the middle?
item.description: Extremism is failing us all. With the heightened political climate in our country and state, we are witnessing increased polarization.

item.title: Federal Border Patrol agent is arrested, accused of drunken driving in Twin Cities on Tuesday
item.description: A federal Border Patrol agent was arrested on suspicion of driving drunk while assigned in Minnesota during the White House’s long-running immigration crackdown.

item.title: Memories: Wonderful restaurants of past, present
item.description: It was a Friday fall evening in the mid-1950s. We had attended a movie at the Broadway Theater and it was time to go home, but we weren’t ready to end the evening. The perfect solution? The Big Dipper. A hamburger/ice cream restaurant on South Broadway — strawberry soda only 20 cents.

item.title: Live United: Collaboration brings strong, long-lasting programs
item.description: Collaboration is a tried and true buzzword in the nonprofit community. I use it all the time to describe the work that we do. I also have strong feelings about what collaboration in programs truly means.

item.title: April Jeppson: The value of time — what do we make of it?
item.description: It is easy to get bogged down in the day-to-day. We stress about all the things — the car making a funny noise, the meeting that ran too long or the never-ending pile of laundry. We spend so much time worrying or stressing that we often forget to look at what’s right in front of us.

item.title: Community plans burger basket benefit for Alden woman with Stage 4 lung cancer
item.description: Alden native Erin Bremseth has never been a smoker and never been exposed to second-hand smoke, yet around Thanksgiving, she was diagnosed with Stage 4 lung cancer.
